memory_update.text: PLPC should be tracked as an underfollowed US-listed transmission-hardware candidate for grid expansion, but its direct tie to HVDC/reactive-power equipment remains unproven and needs product/customer verification.
AMSC is the cleanest US-listed small-cap candidate found for dynamic reactive-power compensation and voltage-control systems through D-VAR/STATCOM-type grid-stability products.

POWL is a second-order electrical infrastructure candidate, more tied to engineered switchgear and power-control systems than to HVDC reactors or capacitors directly; keep but require backlog/end-market proof.

HUBB is a useful reference benchmark for public utility T&D component exposure, including bushings, arresters, insulators, connectors, switches and grid controls, but it is not the underfollowed lane target.

The most node-pure names for HVDC reactors, CTC magnet wire, high-voltage reactive-power compensation and power-quality equipment may be non-US-listed or private; US-listed exposure appears more indirect and requires follow-up on product-level revenue.

node: HVDC reactors, high-voltage reactive power compensation, capacitors, bushings, magnet wire, and specialized grid-stability equipment
summary: Layer 1B expansion found a narrow US-listed universe with plausible exposure to high-voltage grid stability and transmission hardware. The cleanest underfollowed candidates are PLPC for transmission-line hardware and AMSC for dynamic reactive-power / voltage-control systems. POWL is a second-order electrical-infrastructure candidate tied to power distribution and control systems rather than HVDC reactors directly. HUBB is included only as a reference anchor because its Utility Solutions segment includes grid T&D components such as bushings, arresters, insulators, connectors, anchors, switches, controls, meters, and substation/transmission products, but it is larger and less pure.
